chapter: Ory, Mutt and New Orleans life
title: Church music and religion in New Orleans
summary: Hall went to Baptist church and Sunday school as a child, later became Catholic, and discusses church music and Creole Catholics.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: I was going to ask about any of the church music you might have heard, and if you belonged to any church when you were in New Orleans.
Well, I used to go to Baptist church, you know. But since I came from California, I turned Catholic.
Most of the people downtown, they were Catholics. Oh, yeah, oh, yeah. I wonder if you were uptown if you were Baptist.

No, the biggest majority, well, the biggest majority of people in y'all was Catholic. That's right. That's all over, I guess. Oh, yeah, the biggest majority of people. I'd say nine percent of people. I suppose. And y'all needs to be Catholic, especially all drill people. Yeah, that's right. They were all Catholic.
Had you heard much music when you were a child in the churches?
No, not so much. Organs and things like that, you know. When I'd go, when we were kids, we had to go to Sunday school, see.
Because I remember Bud Scott and I think Mutt, too, had told us when they were children that there was good music that had that good beat in the churches.
Yeah, they kept a very good beat even in the churches.
